title: Where are the 'most beautiful' campgrounds in California? See where to stay - NewsBreak
text:
By Alexiah Syrai Olsen ,
21 hours ago Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park and Yosemite National Park have some of the best places to camp in California. KEITH WALKLET/Yosemite Conservancy/Special to The Bee Looking for a campground with a view?
Architectural Digest recently highlighted five of the “ most beautiful” places to camp in California .
“Spanning redwood forests and star-strewn deserts, these campgrounds make the case for trading your bed for a sleeping bag,” the publication said.
California is home to nine national parks — more than any other state — and 280 state parks .
Here’s where to find the most stunning camping spots:
The Pfeiffer Falls Trail in California’s Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park. Max Whittaker/Save the Redwoods League What’s the most beautiful place to camp on Central Coast? According to Architectural Digest, the campground at Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park is among the most scenic places to camp in California in 2026.
Home to an “ extremely popular campground ,” the Big Sur park features “an exquisite mix of forest, waterfalls and coastal scenery in one place,” The Tribune previously reported.
The Big Sur River winds through redwood, oak, sycamore and willow trees, while the Santa Lucia mountains tower high over the gorge.
The park’s campground offers “premium sites that sit directly along the river,” Architectural Digest said.
Architectural Digest named Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park one of the most beautiful places in the United States .
Reservations at Big Sur’s largest campground can be made up to six months in advance.
It costs $50 per night to stay at a standard campsite, while a premium riverfront site costs $60 a night to reserve.
In both cases, your reservation fee includes entry for two vehicles and up to six people per campsite.
Where should I camp at Yosemite National Park? Yosemite National Park also has one of the most beautiful campgrounds in California, according to Architectural Digest.
“With views of Half Dome and Yosemite Falls ... right from the campground, it’s clear that North Pines belongs on this list,” the publication said. “Fall asleep to the soothing sounds of the creek, then wake up to a canopy of ponderosa pines and the dramatic granite cliffs of the Sierra Nevada ...”
Nestled in the Sierra Nevada, Yosemite National Park features waterfalls, meadows, giant sequioas and granite cliffs spread across 748,542 acres.
According to the National Park Service, Yosemite was the most popular national park in California in 2025, attracting more than 4.2 million visitors.
North Pines Campground is “centrally located in the park and boasts some of Yosemite’s most iconic features ,” the National Park Service said.
Reservations for the campground along the Merced River will be released through a lottery system for early access and general sale dates from February to May. Early access lottery tickets cost $10, and reservations are $36 per night.
Each campsite can hold up to six people and a maximum of two vehicles.
Roosevelt elk are a tempting target for photographers in Prairie Creek Redwood State Park. Sacramento Bee Staff Photo What’s the most beautiful campground in Northern California? In Humboldt County, Prairies Creek Redwoods State Park boasts one of the prettiest places to camp in California: Elk Prairie Campground.
“Old-growth redwood forests surround the campground, and a prehistoric-looking gorge with 50-foot walls covered in ferns is just 10 miles away,” Archtectural Digest said.
The park features “sandy beaches and open meadows grazed by magnificent herds of Roosevelt elk,” the National Park Service said.
It’s also home to the world’s largest living tree species, the coast redwood.
Elk Prairie Campground has both cabins and campsites to rent online.
Each cabin can fit up to six people, with additional camping space outside for two more guests. Cabins, which include one vehicle entry, start at $100 per night.
Campsites hold up to eight people and two cars apiece, with prices starting at $5 per night.
Joshua Tree National Park’s Jumbo Rocks campground is among the most beautiful in California, Architectural Digest says. Photo by Explore with Joshua via Unsplash What are the best campgrounds in Southern California? “For beach bums, it doesn’t get any better than Moro Campground in Laguna Beach’s Crystal Cove State Park ,” Architectural Digest said.
Campsites sit on top of bluffs and have direct access to the water.
Moro Campground has 27 RV hookup sites, 30 tent sites and 32 campsites that can only be reached by hiking.
Hike-in campsites can fit up to four people, while the other sites can hold a maximum of eight.
Reservations can be made online, with prices starting at $55 per night.
Jumbo Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park also landed on Architectural Digest’s list of the most beautiful campgrounds in California.
Architectural Digest said Jumbo Rocks is “blessed with magnificently massive boulders that’ll make it feel like you’ve blasted off to another planet rather than settled into the desert.”
Top activities include stargazing and hiking the park’s trails.
The campground has 124 campsites that cost $30 per night and can fit up to six people, three tents and one car. If space is available, campers can park two cars.
Senior or access pass reservations cost $15 per night. Reservations can be made online .
summary: Home to an “ extremely popular campground ,” the Big Sur park features “an exquisite mix of forest, waterfalls and coastal scenery in one place,” The Tribune previously reported. The Big Sur River winds through redwood, oak, sycamore and willow trees, while the Santa Lucia mountains tower high over the gorge. “Old-growth redwood forests surround the campground, and a prehistoric-looking gorge with 50-foot walls covered in ferns is just 10 miles away,” Archtectural Digest said. Jumbo Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park also landed on Architectural Digest’s list of the most beautiful campgrounds in California.
